clips.text_zh: 聯儲局唔會加息。Warsh 出嚟話認真對付通脹，但實際做乜都冇。Bessent 買緊 yen，跟住暗示會拋一萬億美元落嚟。Trump 又鬧 Powell 減息太遲。又係炒吓。命理都話我今年唔好亂開倉🙏
clips.text_en_b1: The Federal Reserve is NOT going to hike. Warsh says they are really serious about inflation, they have a taskforce looking into it, then they continue doing nothing. Bessent's to-do list: buy yen, double Yellen's buybacks, and strongly imply he might dump a trillion dollars on those buybacks. Trump criticizes Powell for not cutting rates because the economy is so good.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread mocking the Fed's inflation theater

signal.rationale: OP implies dollar weakness from Bessent's intervention and Trump demanding cuts

clips.text_en_b2: The Federal Reserve is hardly about to raise rates, regardless of the noise. Warsh keeps insisting they are finally getting tough on inflation, yet a taskforce is announced and nothing concrete actually follows. Meanwhile, Bessent's agenda seems to boil down to snapping up yen, doubling Yellen's buybacks, and hinting he could unleash a trillion dollars against them. Trump, for his part, hammers Powell for holding off on cuts despite the economy supposedly being so strong. Classic cycle of theatrics, no substance.
clips.text_en_c1: The Federal Reserve will almost certainly refrain from further hikes. Kevin Warsh has publicly committed to tackling inflation with renewed vigour, yet the taskforce assembled for that purpose appears to have produced nothing of substance. Scott Bessent, meanwhile, has been quietly accumulating yen, doubling the buyback operations initiated under Janet Yellen, and hinting rather unsubtly that a one-trillion-dollar intervention might materialise should conditions deteriorate. Donald Trump has separately lambasted Jerome Powell for delaying cuts, arguing that the underlying economy is robust enough to justify immediate easing. Taken in aggregate, these competing signals suggest that traders should anticipate volatility rather than directional conviction.
clips.text_en_c2: Speculation that the Federal Reserve might yet raise rates remains, in this commentator's view, fanciful. Kevin Warsh has publicly intimated that the institution harbours a steely resolve to subdue inflation, having convened a dedicated task force to examine the problem; yet no tangible tightening has materialised, the rhetoric drifting conspicuously into the void. Meanwhile, Scott Bessent's purported agenda appears to involve accumulating yen, doubling Janet Yellen's prior round of buybacks, and darkly hinting that a trillion-dollar deluge might be unleashed against those very positions. Donald Trump, for his part, has lambasted Chair Jerome Powell for tardiness in easing monetary policy, contending that the underlying economy merits such a move forthwith. The observer wryly notes that fortune-telling advises against opening fresh positions this year.

clips.text_zh: 十年長揸你揀 BTC 定黃金？XRP 同 DOGE 真係陪我捱過五個地獄年。CFD 啲帳面真係見唔到光，靠 AI 續命🧐 prop firm 嗰邊又未過 eval。算啦，當交學費。
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin versus gold: if you had to hold only one for the next ten years, which would you choose, and what makes it better than the other? Meanwhile, in one week's time you will know why you held XRP, BTC and DOGE through the toughest five years any investor has ever faced.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread asking which asset to hold for a decade

signal.rationale: OP frames long-term conviction hold; pairs BTC vs gold comparison

clips.text_en_b2: Holding for the long haul raises a genuine dilemma: over the next ten years, would Bitcoin or gold deliver more, and on what grounds? The poster argues the toughest five-year stretch any investor has had to stomach only proved why holding XRP, BTC and DOGE through sheer hell was worth it. Meanwhile, retail traders burned by CFDs and stuck waiting on a prop firm eval can take cold comfort: at least the tuition fee bought something.
clips.text_en_c1: If one were compelled to select a single asset for the next decade, would Bitcoin or gold represent the more compelling proposition, and what fundamental characteristics would inform that decision? Proponents of the former cite its asymmetric upside and decentralised architecture, whereas traditionalists maintain that bullion's millennia-long track record confers an almost irreplaceable store-of-value function. The original poster, evidently nursing losses from CFD positions that have yet to break even, defends his conviction in XRP, Bitcoin and DOGE, all of which he held throughout what he describes as five harrowing years for any retail investor. Prop firm evaluations remain pending, and the AI-assisted trading experiment continues to underperform.
clips.text_en_c2: Were one compelled to select a single asset for an entire decade of unwavering conviction, would it be Bitcoin or gold that one entrusts with such stewardship, and what intrinsic attribute renders it superior to its rival? The poster contends that within merely seven days the rationale for weathering the most punishing five-year crucible any contemporary investor has endured whilst holding XRP, BTC and DOGE will become resplendently apparent. Margin accounts have languished in perpetual deficit, sustained only by artificially inflated AI-generated valuations, whilst proprietary trading evaluations remain obstinately incomplete. The poster concedes, with philosophical equanimity, that these tribulations ought to be regarded as tuition rather than catastrophe.

clips.text_zh: OpenAI 又出事了。兩個數學家用 claude 同 gpt 合作解難題，OpenAI 就話自己個 agent swarm 獨立解咗。連 credit 都冇俾。靠 AI 續命嘅廢柴如我，睇到都驚。日後連考牌都可能被 AI 代我答🙏
clips.text_en_b1: OpenAI steals a math breakthrough. Mathematicians Alpage and Buckmaster collaborated using Claude and GPT and made good progress. OpenAI then claimed an agent swarm solved the problem independently, with an approach very similar to their work. The mathematicians were not credited in the paper.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on OpenAI allegedly taking credit for math work

signal.rationale: Not a trade, AI industry observation

clips.text_en_b2: OpenAI finds itself in hot water once again. Mathematicians Alpage and Buckmaster had been collaborating through Claude and GPT and were making solid headway on a stubborn problem. Shortly afterwards, OpenAI put out a paper claiming its agent swarm cracked the same challenge independently, using an approach suspiciously close to theirs. No credit whatsoever was given to the original pair, and the community is rightly calling it out as outright theft of intellectual work.
clips.text_en_c1: OpenAI stands accused of appropriating a mathematical breakthrough that ought to have belonged to its collaborators. Mathematicians Alpage and Buckmaster had been making considerable headway on a notoriously intractable problem using Claude and GPT in tandem, refining hypotheses iteratively across multiple sessions. OpenAI subsequently asserted that an internal agent swarm had solved the very same problem autonomously, employing an approach strikingly reminiscent of the pair's published methodology. The mathematicians received no acknowledgement whatsoever in the resulting paper, a striking omission given the documented overlap in reasoning.
clips.text_en_c2: OpenAI has once again found itself mired in controversy, after two mathematicians, working in concert with Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's own GPT, achieved meaningful progress on a recalcitrant problem. OpenAI subsequently alleged that an autonomous agent swarm had independently arrived at the solution, employing a methodology strikingly homologous to that of the human researchers. The mathematicians, it transpires, received no acknowledgement whatsoever in the published paper. Observers dependent upon AI to perpetuate otherwise untenable workflows confess to genuine disquiet at such appropriations, wondering whether professional examinations themselves may soon be similarly outsourced. The episode casts an unflattering pall upon prevailing notions of intellectual attribution.

Hip-hop promotion and Nike-aligned narratives, the poster contends, have withered virtually overnight, as though funding streams had been abruptly severed. The commentator observes, with characteristic detachment, that such grand stratagems scarcely impinge upon those whose media diet consists exclusively of local Hong Kong forums and financial boards.

clips.text_en_b1: Does no one find it suspicious that the developer is not listed anywhere in the trailer, website, or promotional materials? The poster asks who Nintendo outsourced the new project to, since the studio name appears nowhere in any official materials.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread on an unannounced Nintendo developer
clips.text_en_b2: Does nobody else find it genuinely suspicious that the developer's name appears absolutely nowhere? The trailer, the official site, every piece of promotional material released so far, and still no studio credit. The poster wonders aloud whether Nintendo has outsourced the project to an unannounced partner or is deliberately keeping things under wraps until launch. The guessing game has officially overtaken any actual hype around the title itself.
clips.text_en_c1: Is it not somewhat conspicuous that Nintendo's most recent trailer makes no reference whatsoever to the studio entrusted with development? Neither the official website, nor the accompanying promotional materials, nor any press release identifies the outsourcing partner responsible for the project, a silence that has predictably ignited considerable speculation across enthusiast forums. Season fifteen of the prevailing competitive league has, by the poster's own admission, grown rather stale, leaving fans to derive what entertainment they can from deciphering corporate mysteries. Several plausible candidates have been floated, ranging from established second-party collaborators to entirely unannounced studios, though Nintendo's characteristic opacity renders any definitive attribution essentially impossible at this juncture.
clips.text_en_c2: Does nobody else find it mildly disquieting that Nintendo's freshly unveiled trailer fails to disclose the development studio anywhere within its duration, accompanying website, or supplementary promotional collateral? The conspicuous omission, deliberate or otherwise, has ignited considerable conjecture within the community regarding the identity of the outsourced partner entrusted with the project. Forum denizens have pored over every frame, hunted through metadata, and scoured press releases, yet the studio's name remains conspicuously absent from any official artefact. Season fifteen of competitive play has stagnated into torpor; speculative threads such as this one, the poster concedes, provide the only present solace against terminal boredom.

clips.text_zh: 有 fit 板膠膠噏話深蹲係現代 lifting 神話，古希臘人都唔做。佢話 bench、OHP、DL 加跑步已經夠練腿。肥仔信今日又叫我 squat，睇完呢個 post 我有藉口偷懶lol🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Squats are a meme lift, prioritized way too much in modern lifting. The poster says the ancient Greeks never did squats, they just ran and carried heavy things. He argues bench, overhead press, deadlift, running, and carrying heavy stuff are all you need to train like the best athletes in history.
clips.text_en_b2: Squats have become something of a meme exercise in modern lifting culture, prioritised far beyond what the movement actually delivers. The poster argues that ancient Greek athletes never touched a squat bar, relying instead on running, carrying heavy loads, and the basics. In his view, combining bench press, overhead press, deadlift, running, and loaded carries is more than enough to train like the greatest athletes history has produced. Apparently, skipping leg day just got a legitimate defence.
clips.text_en_c1: A contentious thread on the fitness board has reignited an enduring debate by characterising the squat as an overemphasised artefact of contemporary strength culture rather than a genuinely indispensable movement. The original poster contends that ancient Greek athletes, whose physiques remain objects of admiration, never performed barbell squats in any recognisable form, relying instead on sprinting, loaded carries and unstructured physical labour. He proposes that bench press, overhead press, deadlift, running and the transportation of heavy objects constitute a sufficient regimen for those aspiring to historic athletic excellence. Critics counter that bilateral lower-body hypertrophy requires dedicated loading patterns unavailable through carries alone.
clips.text_en_c2: A fitness enthusiast has provocatively characterised the barbell back squat as a contemporary lifting myth, disproportionately venerated within modern strength culture despite, he insists, a complete absence of corroboration in antiquity. The Greeks, he contends, never performed the movement as such; their celebrated physiques were forged instead through running, overhead pressing, and the patient carriage of substantial loads over considerable distances. He maintains that bench press, overhead press, deadlift, distance running, and weighted carries constitute the entirety of what any aspiring athlete requires to approximate the conditioning of history's finest. He confesses, with endearing candour, that the thread has furnished him the perfect pretext to abscond from today's scheduled session.
